title: Habibsters Rule the Range: Kaushal Wins Buckaroo Bowl I as Ben Dover Rides the Ladder to the Bottom
dek: The league's first season ended with Kaushal holding the trophy, Alan holding the season's best single week, Mekhi holding the most points and nothing to show for it, and Sonny holding the very first last-place finish in Buckaroo history.
body: Every dynasty needs a first chapter, and the Buckaroo Football League's opened in 2023 with six teams, one ESPN league and zero idea what was coming. By the time the dust settled, Kaushal's Habibsters had gone 10-4, grabbed the top seed, and won Buckaroo Bowl I by nearly 60 points. Somewhere in the Georgia sky, a college football fan was already planning the parade.

The regular season was a lesson in the gap between scoring points and winning games. Mekhi's Dawgs led the entire league with 1,542.8 points, 14 more than the champion, and still went 6-8. If you ever need proof that fantasy football is a cruel game, frame that stat line and hang it over Kai's desk. Habibsters were nearly as prolific at 1,528.8, but they actually turned the points into wins, which turns out to be the whole idea.

Alan's Team Pillbert finished 9-5 and took the second seed with 1,499.3 points, and Philly also owned the loudest Sunday of the year: 156.18 in Week 3, the highest single-week score in the league. Randy's The fumblers landed the third seed at 7-7, which brings us to the season's most telling number: zero. Not one trade was made across the entire league in 2023, and nobody who knows Randy was surprised that his roster stayed exactly where he put it.

The playoffs were two-week totals, and the top seeds took care of business. Habibsters beat Dawgs 237.54 to 196.12, ending Mekhi's season the same way it had gone all year: plenty of firepower, not enough on the scoreboard that counts. Team Pillbert outlasted The fumblers 234.86 to 216.44 in the closer semifinal, setting up the 1-versus-2 Buckaroo Bowl everyone expected. Randy went on to finish third and Mekhi fourth.

Buckaroo Bowl I was not close. Habibsters put up 251.36 over the two weeks, the biggest total of the postseason, and Team Pillbert managed 192.08, a 59.28-point margin that turned the title game into a coronation. Kaushal, who had the second-best offense all year, saved his best for last. Alan had the league's best single week back in September, but in December the trophy went to the guy who was best when it mattered.

At the other end, the consolation ladder delivered the season's twist. Ramon's Araleasers went 4-10, scored the fewest points in the league at 1,375.3, and posted the lowest single week of the year with 65.9 in Week 9. And yet it was Sonny's Ben Dover, 6-8 and the fifth seed, who finished last after the ladder had its say, while Araleasers climbed to fifth. Being the commissioner who set up the league did not come with any protection from it.

So the first page of the history book reads: Kaushal on top, Sonny on the bottom, and a whole lot of untraded players in between. Ben Dover's last-place finish would not be the end of that story, but in 2023 it was simply the first entry in a long, honest record. Buckaroo Bowl I belongs to the Habibsters, and the rest of the league spent the offseason figuring out how to catch them.
